newsitem.title: USA: Jobless claims drop in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Jobless claims drop in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans lining up to collect unemployment benefits fell last week, while help-wanted advertisements rose in February, two reports released on Thursday showed.

The Labour Department said first-time jobless claims fell to 310,000 in the week ended March 22, compared with a revised 314,000 the previous week. Wall Street economists had forecast 313,000 claims for the latest week.
The four-week moving average of claims, which is considered a better barometer of employment trends because it smooths out volatility in the weekly numbers, fell to 311,250 from a revised 312,750.
The total number of Americans continuing to claim jobless benefits was also down, falling to 2,281,000 in the week ended March 15, the latest week for which that data were available.
That was the lowest level for ongoing claims since the week ended Dec. 9, 1989, when they hit 2,268,000, the department said.
The U.S. help-wanted advertising index rose three points to 90 in February from 87 in January, according to the Conference Board, a private business group.
"The job market continues to show surprising strength," said Conference Board economist Ken Goldstein.
He said a pickup in employment mixed with slowing job cuts suggests the labour market "is about to become even tighter."
Goldstein said job growth is "unlikely to slow to an average of 200,000 new jobs per month, even with a new and more restrictive monetary policy in place."
Consumer confidence has derived some strength from dominant trends in the labour market, such as sustained job growth and slight advances in hourly compensation, Goldstein added.
Four states reported decreases in jobless claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended March 15, the latest period for which data were available.
They were California, with 5,891 fewer new filings, Pennsylvania, with 2,275, New York, with 1,950 and Ohio, with 1,793.
Pennsylvania reported fewer layoffs in the primary metals, paper, furniture, and lumber and wood industries. The other states had no comment.
Three states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000 in the week ended March 15. They were Arkansas, with 1,528 additional new filings, Tennessee, with 1,319, and North Carolina, with 1,157.

Arkansas said it had layoffs in the trade industry. Tennessee reported layoffs in the food, textile, apparel, furniture, scientific instruments, trade and service industries. North Carolina gave no reason for the increase.

The Conference Board said that in the last three months, the volume of help-wanted advertising rose in six of the nine U.S. regions. The greatest increase was in the Middle Atlantic region, up 16 percent. Other regional increases were in the Pacific, up 6.8 percent; East North Central, up 3.5 percent; and South Atlantic, up 3.2 percent.
Regions with declines were New England, down 9.8 percent; East South Central, down 2.2 percent; and Mountain, down 2.5 percent.
